sections.html:
A Maryland deed is recorded in the land records of the county where the property sits, through the Clerk of the Circuit Court for that county.

Counties differ in how the paperwork reaches the clerk. In Harford County, for example, the Land Records Department in Bel Air takes documents three ways: e-recording through Simplifile, mail, or walk-in. Walk-in customers there are limited to five documents or sets at a time, and recorded papers go back by U.S. Mail unless the customer asks otherwise.

Hours matter on closing day. Harford's land records counter runs 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM on weekdays, with a 4:00 PM cutoff for couriers and title companies. Ask the title company when the deed will actually reach the counter, since a late submission can slow the date you're paid.

  • Recording is county based: use the land records of the county where the house is located.
  • Some counties split the work. Baltimore County sends deeds through its Transfer and Recordation Section before the Circuit Court finalizes them.
  • E-recording through a vendor such as Simplifile is one option, and the clerk can give account details.

sections.h2: What a deed needs before the clerk will record it
sections.html:
The clerk needs a complete intake sheet, proof that taxes are current, and the correct fees and taxes. Without those, the instrument is returned.

Real Property Article 3-104 sets the core rules. A complete intake sheet lists the property identifier, parties, instrument type, consideration, recording charges and taxes, claimed exemptions and the tax bill mailing address. A deed also needs a certification that a Maryland attorney, or a party named in the deed, prepared it. The collector must endorse the deed to show that current taxes and charges are paid.

In Baltimore County, a deed that changes ownership and arrives without a lien certificate won't be processed. Agricultural-use deeds and partial transfer deeds need approval from the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation first, at its Towson office.

You can catch most delays before closing by asking the title company three questions.

  • Is the lien certificate ordered, and does it show any unpaid county or municipal charges?
  • Who prepared the deed, and is the preparer certification signed?
  • Does the intake sheet name the right exemption code, if any is claimed?

sections.h2: What it costs to record a deed
sections.html:
Recording a deed costs a per-document fee plus a flat surcharge, and the taxes are billed on top. The clerk's fee depends mainly on page count and on whether the property is a principal residence. Cecil and Harford counties use the same structure.

ChargeAmount
Release, 9 pages or fewer$10.00
Other instrument, 9 pages or fewer, or principal residence only$20.00
Other instrument, 10 pages or more$75.00
Surcharge on most recordable instruments$40.00
State transfer tax (Cecil and Harford)0.50% of consideration
State transfer tax, first-time Maryland buyer, principal residence0.25%

In Harford, recording fees are non-refundable, while a state transfer tax refund needs a claim form filed with the clerk. Copies cost $0.50 a page there, and certification costs $5.00. Check the page count of the deed, because it decides which tier applies.

sections.h2: Recordation and transfer taxes by county
sections.html:
The state transfer tax is the same everywhere, but recordation tax and county transfer tax change from one county to the next. Get the county's own figure from the title company or the county revenue office.

Baltimore County charges a county transfer tax of 1.5 percent of consideration and a state recordation tax of $2.50 for each $500 or fraction of consideration. Cecil County's clerk lists recordation tax at $4.10 per $500, rounded, of the actual consideration. In Harford County, county transfer tax and recordation tax are collected by the county's Revenue Collections office on South Main Street in Bel Air, and the clerk collects the recording fees and state transfer tax.

Checks may be payable to the Clerk of the Circuit Court, to the county government, or to both, depending on the county. If transfer tax is coming out of your proceeds, ask for a line-by-line estimate before you sign.

  • Baltimore County: payments go to Baltimore County, Maryland, at the Office of Budget and Finance in Towson.
  • Harford County: county taxes go to Harford County Revenue, fees to the Clerk.
  • Cecil County: fees are paid at the Department of Finance.

sections.h2: Exemptions that lower the tax bill
sections.html:
Maryland law lets counties exempt first-time buyers of owner-occupied homes from part of the tax, and it exempts some family and estate transfers entirely. Exemptions must be claimed on the intake sheet. In Harford, a claimed exemption must cite the full exemption code or the full tax is charged.

Under Tax-Property Article 12-103(b), a county or Baltimore City may adopt a recordation tax exemption on a set amount of consideration for owner-occupied residential property, if the buyer will occupy the home for at least 7 months of a 12-month period. A second option covers a person who has never owned a Maryland principal residence and will occupy the property, and each grantee signs a sworn statement. The state transfer tax has a first-time buyer rate of 0.25 percent, with the same sworn statement from each grantee.

Transfers under Maryland's new transfer-on-death deed law are also exempt from state recordation tax, state transfer tax and county transfer tax when the property is the transferor's primary or secondary residence (Chapter 751 of the 2026 laws). Heirs may still owe inheritance tax.

sections.h2: Problems sellers and heirs run into
sections.html:
The recurring problems are missing lien certificates, unpaid taxes, a wrong legal description and an unrecorded prior deed in the chain of title. Each one stops the clerk, or the title company, from closing.

Estate sales add steps, because the intake sheet must name the parties and the instrument type correctly, and the preparer certification still applies to the deed.

Transfers of an entity that owns real estate can also be taxed as if a deed were recorded. Moving more than 80 percent of the equity in an entity that owns real property can trigger recordation tax under Tax-Property 12-117, with transfer tax extended by 13-103. If you hold a rental house in an LLC, check this before selling membership interests.

Nonresident sellers have one more item. Maryland Comptroller withholding on real property sales by nonresidents may apply and is collected by the Clerk.

  • Confirm the legal description matches the last recorded deed.
  • Pay or payoff any county water, sewer or tax charges before the lien certificate is ordered.
  • Ask whether an exemption applies and gather the sworn statements early.
  • For an inherited house, confirm who has authority to sign before the deed is drafted.

A cash sale uses the same recording steps, with fewer moving parts. With no lender, there is no new deed of trust to record beside the deed, and the file usually closes once the title company confirms the lien certificate and taxes.

You still sign a deed, and the clerk still receives the intake sheet and collects the fees. Cash Home Buyers can buy houses in Maryland as-is, including homes with open liens or title questions that need to be cleared at closing. Because the deed has to be recorded to complete the transfer, ask the title company when the recording is scheduled and who is paying each tax line.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Maryland?
faqs.a: With the Clerk of the Circuit Court in the county where the property is located. Many counties accept e-recording, mail and walk-in filing, and some route deeds through a county revenue office first.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Maryland?
faqs.a: The clerk's fee is $20 for most deeds of nine pages or fewer and $75 for ten pages or more, plus a $40 surcharge. Transfer and recordation taxes are charged separately and vary by county.

faqs.q: What is the Maryland state transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: The state rate in Cecil and Harford is 0.50 percent of the consideration, or 0.25 percent for a first-time Maryland buyer who will use the home as a principal residence. Sworn statements are required for the lower rate.

faqs.q: Can a deed be recorded without a lien certificate?
faqs.a: Generally no. Real Property Article 3-104 requires the collector's certificate for a change-of-ownership instrument, and Baltimore County won't process a deed without one.

faqs.q: Does a transfer-on-death deed need to be recorded?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Chapter 751 of the 2026 laws, a transfer-on-death deed is effective only if it is recorded in the county land records before the owner dies.
